hero.lead: A mountain nation of 10.8 million where citizens abroad send home more than half the economy, rivers give 93% of the power, and the World Bank has backed the Rogun dam with $350 million in 2024 and $300 million in 2026.

capital.heading: Rogun and the remittances: two flows to build a nation.

register.name: Resilient Water Systems for All (RWS4All)
register.detail: Green Climate Fund · approved 2 July 2026 at the 45th Board meeting · accredited entity EBRD · GCF grant for the two nations together · total $179M with $112M of loan co-financing · FP309
register.note: Shared with the Kyrgyz Republic: around 621,100 people directly and 1.2 million indirectly across both nations
register.text: A Green Climate Fund grant programme for water utilities in the Kyrgyz Republic and Tajikistan: climate risk assessment, adaptation pathways and priority resilient infrastructure, with EBRD loans for water supply, wastewater and irrigation. It bears directly on the water standard, the furthest from reach in Tajikistan.

register.name: Second Strengthening Water and Irrigation Management Project (SWIM-2)
register.detail: World Bank (IDA) · approved 1 July 2026 · IDA grant · the OPEC Fund and the Islamic Development Bank have each pledged $50M · project P515852
register.note: Irrigation for 100,000 hectares and about 470,000 farmers and rural community members; bulk drinking water supply for 170,000 people
register.text: An IDA grant to rehabilitate and modernise irrigation, including at least 20 pumping stations, the Dangara diversion tunnel and the Beshkent hydrotechnical facility, and to strengthen Water User Associations. It carries the food and livelihood standards for about 470,000 farmers and rural people, and its programme paper provides for bulk drinking water supply for 170,000 people.

register.name: Second Competitive and Inclusive Tajikistan Development Policy Operation
register.detail: World Bank (IDA) · approved 1 July 2026 · IDA grant · budget support
register.note: Budget support paid against reforms; not earmarked to any one standard
register.text: An IDA grant to the state budget, paid against reforms in competition, state aid, state-owned enterprises, the investment climate and energy tariffs. The government has revised its methodology for targeted social assistance and publishes budget spending for schools and primary health care facilities, which bears on the livelihood, education and health standards; the funds are not earmarked.

register.name: Second Phase of Sustainable Financing for Rogun Hydropower Project
register.detail: World Bank (IDA) · approved 30 June 2026 · IDA grant of SDR 219.2M ($300M equivalent) · project P513856
register.note: The second phase of a programme estimated at $6.29bn; ten other lenders are named as expected co-financiers of the phase
register.text: An IDA grant for civil works, generating equipment and implementation support at the Rogun hydropower plant on the Vakhsh river, including safety, environmental and social measures. The World Bank expects the project to give 10 million people in Tajikistan improved access to affordable, reliable and sustainable electricity and to create over 30,000 jobs, which carries the energy and livelihood standards.

register.name: Tajikistan Women’s Economic Empowerment Project (TWEEP)
register.detail: World Bank · approved 1 May 2026 · grant from the Japan Social Development Fund · project P511398
register.note: For up to 20,000 people; 850 women-owned and women-led businesses to gain access to financial services
register.text: A trust-fund grant for entrepreneurship training, skills and access to finance for women, the unemployed and rural and peri-urban residents in Dushanbe, the Districts of Republican Subordination and Gorno-Badakhshan. It carries the livelihood standard, with 3,450 new jobs expected.

register.name: First Competitive and Inclusive Tajikistan Development Policy Operation
register.detail: World Bank (IDA) · approved 7 August 2025 · IDA grant · budget support · project P501015
register.note: Budget support paid against reforms; not earmarked to any one standard
register.text: An IDA grant to the state budget in support of reforms that open the economy to competition, under the National Development Strategy 2030. It is the first of the series continued in July 2026 and is not earmarked to any one of the seven standards.

register.name: Socio-Economic Resilience Strengthening Project, additional financing
register.detail: World Bank (IDA) · approved 6 June 2025 · IDA grant · project P168052
register.note: Faizobod, Nurobod and Danghara districts, Rogun and Tursunzoda cities, and Qubodiyon and Roshtqal’a districts
register.text: An IDA grant that extends a community infrastructure project: the rehabilitation of schools, health clinics and water supply systems, with renewable energy and training in entrepreneurship. It carries the water, education, health and livelihood standards in the districts and cities it reaches.

register.name: Sustainable Financing for Rogun Hydropower Project
register.detail: World Bank (IDA) · approved 17 December 2024 · financing agreement of 18 December 2024 for SDR 258.1M, amended 22 December 2025 · project P181029
register.note: The first phase of a multiphase programme; a second phase of $300M was approved on 30 June 2026
register.text: The first phase of World Bank financing for the Rogun dam and hydropower plant on the Vakhsh river, with a projected installed capacity of 3,780 MW. It carries the energy standard; its second phase followed in June 2026.

register.name: Tajikistan Millati Solim Project
register.detail: World Bank · Approved 24 October 2023
register.text: Health and nutrition for a healthy nation.

register.name: Financial and Private Sector Development Project
register.detail: World Bank · Approved 10 July 2023
register.text: Finance for private firms.

register.name: Social Insurance System Modernization and Digitalization Project
register.detail: ADB · approved 2 October 2026 · grant: $19.5M from the Asian Development Fund, including $12.32M from ADB’s Middle East conflict support package, and $1M from the High-Level Technology Fund · project 59011-001
register.note: Faster and more secure services for at least 320,000 existing contributors and 250,000 pensioners
register.text: An ADB grant to modernise and digitise the Agency of Social Insurance and Pension and to extend pension coverage to informal and self-employed workers, labour migrants and their families. It carries the livelihood standard, and it helps women enrol and connects them with maternal health care.

register.name: Integrated Regional Health Security and Primary Healthcare Services Project
register.detail: ADB · approved 22 September 2026 · $28M Asian Development Fund grant · $10.27M Pandemic Fund grant · $3M Japan Fund for Prosperous and Resilient Asia and the Pacific · $2M Green Climate Fund · project 59108-001
register.note: The first project ADB has approved under the Glaciers to Farms Program
register.text: A grant package to strengthen disease surveillance at major border crossings, upgrade public health laboratories and reform primary health care in rural, remote and border areas, with five integrated service centres for survivors of violence against women and girls. It carries the health standard.

register.name: Budget support loan
register.detail: Eurasian Fund for Stabilization and Development · signed 13 August 2026 in Dushanbe · 20 years with a ten-year grace period · 1% a year · three tranches in 2026 and 2027
register.note: Budget support under the macroeconomic stabilisation programme for 2025-2027; not earmarked to any one standard
register.text: A concessional loan to the state budget, paid in three tranches against twelve programme measures in macroeconomic stability, fiscal policy and transparency. Its proceeds finance budget expenditures, including the maintenance of priority social spending.
by: Eurasian Fund for Stabilization and Development

register.name: Dushanbe Urban Water Resilience Project
register.detail: ADB · proposed · concept cleared 15 December 2025 · fact-finding 14 to 25 September 2026 · $8M Asian Development Fund grant and $30M concessional loan · project 58344-001
register.note: Executing agency: the State Executive Authority of Dushanbe City; implementing agency: Dushanbevodokanal
register.text: A proposed ADB grant and concessional loan to make the water supply of Dushanbe, a city of 1.0 million people in 2022, more resilient. The Samotechnaya intake alone supplies about 30% of the city’s population, so the project bears directly on the water standard.

register.name: Digital Agriculture Management for Improved Food Security Project
register.detail: ADB · approved 21 November 2025 · $14M Asian Development Fund grant and $3M from the Japan Fund for Prosperous and Resilient Asia and the Pacific · completion targeted for 2031 · project 57307-001
register.note: Includes scholarships for women veterinarians and a national network of women veterinarians
register.text: A grant to modernise livestock farming with a national digital system that tracks animal health and livestock movement, better breeding and veterinary services and digital pasture mapping. Most livestock is raised by small households, so it carries the food and livelihood standards.

register.name: Rogun Hydropower Development Project, Phase 1
register.detail: AIIB · approved 19 December 2024 · sovereign loan · Phase 1 of a $500M multiphase programme · co-financed with the World Bank · project 000687
register.note: Rogun’s projected installed capacity is 3,780 MW
register.text: An AIIB loan for the first phase of a multiphase programme to help Tajikistan complete the Rogun hydropower plant, co-financed with the World Bank. AIIB states that the plant will improve electricity access for about 10 million people, which carries the energy standard.

register.name: Golovnaya 240-Megawatt Hydropower Plant Rehabilitation Project, additional financing
register.detail: ADB · approved 6 August 2024 · grant · project 46418-002
register.note: Capacity expected to rise from 240 MW in 2012 to 274 MW by 2026
register.text: An ADB grant to replace generating unit 4 at the Golovnaya hydropower plant, which stopped in 2019 after mechanical damage. It adds clean power to the national and regional grids, which carries the energy standard.

register.name: Dushanbe Water Supply and Sanitation Project
register.detail: ADB · grant of $41.18M approved 27 September 2018 · additional grant of $38M approved 29 August 2022 · closing 31 March 2028 · project 50347-002
register.note: An older instrument, still active and material for water; the amount is the sum of the two grants (arithmetic)
register.text: ADB grants from the Asian Development Fund to improve water supply and sanitation in Dushanbe, benefitting 352,000 people, among them 100,000 residents of the Shohmanshur and Rudaki districts. It carries the water standard, the furthest from reach in Tajikistan.

register.name: Construction of the Substation for the Bulk Power System in Dushanbe City
register.detail: JICA · grant agreement signed 21 October 2026 in Dushanbe · up to ¥3,296M · a new 220 kV transmission substation
register.note: A grant for equipment, installation and consulting services
register.text: A Japanese grant for the equipment and installation of a new 220 kV transmission substation for the bulk power system of Dushanbe. It makes the capital’s power supply more reliable, which carries the energy standard.

register.name: Local-currency loan to Bank Arvand
register.detail: IFC · announced 8 September 2025 · in somoni · for micro and small businesses, housing and energy efficiency
register.note: Bank Arvand serves more than 58,000 borrowers throughout the country
register.text: An IFC loan in local currency so that Bank Arvand can lend more to entrepreneurs, women-owned and rural firms, and give microloans to low-income families to build new homes or renovate existing ones. It carries the shelter and livelihood standards.

assets.heading: Five assets no balance sheet counts.

items.name: The Clean Grid
items.label: Of electricity from renewable sources, 2021
items.text: Rivers give 93% of the power; Rogun will add more to sell across Central Asia.

items.name: The Diaspora
items.label: Of GDP sent home by citizens abroad, 2025
items.text: Tajiks working abroad send home more than half the economy.

items.name: The Fresh Water
items.label: Renewable fresh water a person, 2022
items.text: Glaciers and the headwaters of Central Asia’s great rivers.

items.name: The Minerals
items.label: Of GDP from mineral rents, 2021
items.text: Metals of the Pamir and Fann mountains: mineral rents worth 7% of the economy.

items.name: The People
items.label: Citizens, 2025
items.text: 35.9% are under fifteen: the workforce and the market of the next generation.

items.name: Pamir Energy
items.text: A company of the Aga Khan Fund for Economic Development that runs power generation, transmission and distribution in Gorno-Badakhshan under a 25-year concession and provides energy for about 99 percent of the province’s population, with subsidies for the poorest.

items.name: IMON International
items.text: A leading microfinance institution, begun as the Imon Fund in 1999 and a bank since December 2025, that lends to farm and women-owned micro and small enterprises and for energy-efficient housing.

items.name: Humo
items.text: A microfinance deposit-taking institution with 24 branches and 49 microfinance service centres that lends to self-employed women, women-owned and rural micro and small enterprises and for micro housing.

items.name: FINCA Tajikistan
items.text: A microfinance organisation that helps its clients improve their quality of life, increase assets and create new jobs, and that the National Bank placed second in its 2025 competition for financial services to women entrepreneurs, for its FINCA Women’s Club.

items.name: Rushdi Kuhiston
items.text: A community-owned micro-loan organisation that since 2016 has lent more than TJS 46 million ($4 million) to more than 7,000 clients, among them over 2,000 women and 2,500 young people.
